scope: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local model benchmark or provider execution
notes: F identifiers supplement E01-E31; F17/F18/F19 explicitly recheck E02/E05/E08 and are not independent new experiments.
Publication/revision dates are not access dates. Mutable documentation does not prove account entitlement.
Abstract-only entries support only the stated high-level findings, not unexamined tables or complete-method verification.
External benchmark claims are not reproduced. Source existence, product functionality and performance superiority are separate claims.
Metadata follow-up: full F11/F13 titles and F13 submission history checked against arXiv abstract pages; F13 currently lists v1 only.

sources.title: Microsoft Researcher: Critique and Council
sources.inspection: article sections on Researcher
sources.claim: Critique separates generation from evaluation using Anthropic and OpenAI models; Council compares outputs side by side. Microsoft reports a 13.8% DRACO improvement.
sources.limits: Vendor evaluation, not independently reproduced here. 13.8% must not be relabeled percentage points. Mutable article contains a later availability banner; launch availability is not current entitlement. Linked technical-community article could not be read.

sources.title: Perplexity Model Council
sources.inspection: full feature and allowance text
sources.locator: How Model Council works; How Computer differs from web
sources.claim: Default frontier lineup spans Anthropic, OpenAI and Google. Web uses three models; Computer allows two to eight independent researchers, synthesis and individual reports. Computer credits differ from web query allowance.
sources.limits: Feature evidence, not an accuracy benchmark. Product is not a bridge reusing the user's three vendor subscriptions. No fixed current model IDs inferred.

sources.title: Perplexity Computer effort mode
sources.inspection: effort selection and spending-limit sections
sources.locator: How effort mode works; Effort mode and credits
sources.claim: Effort selects coordinating model and reasoning level; it is not a step, tool or spending cap. Model-to-setting mappings can change.
sources.limits: Does not expose full supporting-agent configuration. Product behavior is not this repository's implementation.

sources.title: karpathy/llm-council
sources.inspection: README and council.py lines 1-200; static, not executed
sources.claim: Independent initial calls, anonymized ranking and chairman synthesis through OpenRouter. Inspected code sends one common ranking list to all models, includes their own successful draft, and reveals model names to the chairman. Failed initial calls are omitted from successful results.
sources.limits: Author labels it an unsupported weekend prototype. Anonymization does not prove bias removal; no randomization or exclusion of own answer in inspected stage2. API route, not subscription CLI integration. No production safety or quality guarantee.

sources.title: PAL clink CLI bridge and Codex preset
sources.inspection: current clink documentation; pinned Codex JSON preset
sources.claim: Connects native Codex, Claude Code and Gemini CLI contexts. Shipped preset includes dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox; documentation warns about relaxed permissions and forwarding conversation history.
sources.limits: Fresh subprocess is not automatically blind when history is forwarded. No agy compatibility, current CLI flag compatibility, safe cancellation or subscription funding preservation tested. Prompt guardrails are not an OS sandbox.

sources.title: PAL consensus tool
sources.inspection: 2026-09-22 follow-up: pinned documentation and static provider-resolution/call-path inspection; no runtime execution
sources.claim: Consensus gathers stance-specific views. Its inspected call path resolves ModelProviderRegistry and calls provider.generate_content; it does not delegate to clink. The code excludes thinking_mode from the exposed schema and passes medium, despite documentation advertising a choice.
sources.limits: The demonstration is hypothetical. API/custom-endpoint transport is not native subscription CLI reuse; a custom endpoint can be local and need not incur paid API charges. Actual billing, provider interpretation of medium, installed-version behavior and agy compatibility were not executed.

sources.title: ReConcile: Round-Table Conference Improves Reasoning via Consensus among Diverse LLMs
sources.inspection: abstract and HTML methodology/evaluation sections
sources.locator: discussion prompt; confidence-weighted voting; model-diversity experiments
sources.claim: Tests multi-model discussion, explanations and confidence-weighted voting on seven benchmarks; reports benefits from model diversity.
sources.limits: Historical model/task settings, not September 2026 frontier CLI collaboration. The paper reweights self-reported confidence using task observations; this is not transferable calibration for our workload and must not be copied into a safety gate.

sources.title: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
sources.inspection: HTML sections 2 and 3, Table 2
sources.claim: Layered proposer/aggregator architecture. Table 2 reports 65.1% LC win rate for MoA versus 57.5% for GPT-4 Omni, with three-run variation for MoA.
sources.limits: Preference win rate is not factual accuracy or coding pass rate. Historical open-model ensemble; extra inference and aggregation remain. Table and introductory headline values differ for the GPT-4o-aggregator variant; that variant's headline is not used here.

sources.title: Breaking Mental Set to Improve Reasoning through Diverse Multi-Agent Debate
sources.inspection: abstract only
sources.claim: DMAD distinguishes reasoning-method diversity from merely assigning personas and reports improved MAD performance with fewer rounds.
sources.limits: No numerical table or code execution verified in this session. Does not prove that vendor diversity alone provides independent errors.

sources.title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
sources.inspection: proceedings abstract; PDF link retrieval failed
sources.claim: Debate does not reliably outperform self-consistency/ensembling by default; tuned protocols can improve and surpass evaluated alternatives.
sources.limits: Neither blanket endorsement nor blanket rejection of debate. No numerical result from the unread PDF is used.

sources.title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
sources.inspection: abstract; HTML rendering contained abstract and references only
sources.locator: abstract: five methods, nine benchmarks, four base models
sources.claim: Reports that many MAD methods fail to outperform CoT/self-consistency despite extra inference; examines heterogeneous models as an improvement direction.
sources.limits: Full experiment tables were not verified. The authors' strong universality wording is not adopted as a general guarantee.

sources.title: Talk Isn't Always Cheap: Understanding Failure Modes in Multi-Agent Debate
sources.inspection: HTML experimental setup and reported debate failures
sources.claim: Mixed-ability debate can propagate mistakes and move initially correct participants to wrong answers. Studies GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B settings.
sources.limits: Not an experiment involving three current frontier products. Workshop status must not be described as ICML main-conference acceptance. Results are conditional, not proof that all debate fails.

sources.title: Preserving Disagreement: Architectural Heterogeneity and Coherence Validation in Multi-Agent Policy Simulation
sources.inspection: HTML setup and disagreement/coherence discussion; abstract version history
sources.locator: 120 deliberations; two policy scenarios; model heterogeneity
sources.claim: Studies preserving disagreement rather than forcing consensus in policy deliberation.
sources.limits: Small local-model-heavy experiment, mostly 7-9B, with a separate coherence validator. Normative disagreement is not a factual-answer benchmark. A single exploratory study does not establish universal deliberation behavior.

sources.title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands
sources.inspection: 2026-09-22 follow-up: durable session, harness recovery, sandbox and credential-boundary sections
sources.locator: Decouple the brain from the hands; recovering from harness failure
sources.claim: Separates durable session events, replaceable harness and execution sandbox; discusses independent recovery.
sources.limits: Hosted service design is a reference, not a subscription-compatible dependency. Vendor runtime outcomes not reproduced here.

sources.title: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals
sources.inspection: 2026-09-22 follow-up: resource enforcement comparison, error rates and measurement recommendations
sources.claim: Reports a six-percentage-point spread between infrastructure configurations in its experiment.
sources.limits: Specific vendor experiment, not a universal correction. Record guaranteed CPU/RAM separately from hard kill limits; larger allocations can change feasible strategies as well as infrastructure failure rates.

sources.title: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes
sources.inspection: team structure, testing, bottlenecks and limitations
sources.locator: 16 agents; near 2000 sessions; Evaluation; Make parallelism easy
sources.claim: Reports a large multi-agent compiler experiment at about $20k API cost, with tests and GCC comparison helping partition debugging.
sources.limits: Same-vendor strong-model team, not cross-vendor debate. High spend, human test-harness effort and remaining compiler limitations; not proof of cheaper autonomous production.

sources.title: Codex non-interactive mode — recheck of E02
sources.inspection: Permissions and safety; structured non-interactive output
sources.locator: read-only default; JSON and output schema
sources.claim: Documents codex exec and read-only sandbox default; broader permission modes must be deliberate.
sources.limits: User's installed version and effective configuration not inspected. Native subprocess does not inherit the whole parent UI session.

sources.title: Claude Agent SDK subscription policy — recheck of E05
sources.inspection: June 15 update banner and preserved older content
sources.locator: Update June 15; content below no longer taking effect
sources.claim: Current top update pauses the announced SDK changes; SDK, claude -p and third-party app use still draw from subscription limits for now.
sources.limits: Lower credit table describes a suspended change. Recheck before implementation; no account entitlement or effective auth route verified.

sources.title: Antigravity headless mode — recheck of E08
sources.inspection: headless output, permission and soft-denial sections
sources.claim: Approval failures can be soft-denied while execution exits zero. Workspace reads and writes are auto-allowed under documented defaults.
sources.limits: Headless is not read-only and exit zero is not verification success. agy is not Gemini CLI; no installed-version or OS-level isolation test performed.

sources.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
sources.inspection: abstract and version history
sources.claim: Examines judge biases and limitations alongside agreement with human preferences.
sources.limits: Human-preference agreement is not proof of factual truth. Abstract used for bias categories, not current-model effect sizes.

sources.title: Harness design for long-running application development
sources.inspection: generator/evaluator separation and frontend feedback loop
sources.locator: self-evaluation; Frontend design; Scaling to full-stack coding
sources.claim: Uses separate generation and evaluation, calibrated criteria and browser interaction. Notes that the final iteration is not necessarily the author's preferred one.
sources.limits: Same-provider harness experiment, not cross-vendor causal evidence. Prompt criteria themselves change results; extra rounds consume time. Fresh evaluator alone does not eliminate leniency.

sources.title: Beyond Consensus: Downward Bias and Role Asymmetry in Multi-Agent LLM Judges for Subjective Evaluation
sources.inspection: methods, experimental setup, Tables 1-3 and limitations; no independent replication
sources.claim: In Korean essay and SummEval scoring, a strict/lenient consensus protocol worsened average alignment with human scores versus a single judge; neutral symmetric roles largely recovered it. Cross-model role swaps did not outperform the strongest single baseline.
sources.limits: Two subjective tasks, six judges, one role configuration and four adjustment rounds. Not evidence that all critiques or blind first drafts are harmful. Score masking during later scoring exchanges is different from preserving independent initial answers.

sources.title: Multi-Agent Debate Strategies: Survey, Taxonomy, and Challenges
sources.inspection: scope, search/selection methods, taxonomy, discussion and threats to validity
sources.claim: Maps 141 studies across participants, interaction and agreement dimensions; motivates explicit protocol descriptions for controlled comparisons.
sources.limits: Descriptive taxonomy, not an experiment proving a winning topology. Natural-language scope; narrow Scopus seed query, citation snowballing and partly subjective extraction limit coverage.

sources.title: Adversarial Review: Structured Disagreement for Grounded Agentic Code Review
sources.revision: arXiv v1; accepted to ICML 2026 Workshop on DL4C per arXiv metadata
sources.inspection: protocol, SWE-PRBench/SWE-bench results, failure cases, cost and limitations; no replication
sources.locator: Sections 3.5, 4.1-4.5, 5.1-5.3, 6-7; Appendix A.3 distinguishes protocol variants
sources.claim: A reviewer/critic exchange over frozen code can expose false consensus; separating code-backed objections from unverified concerns improved its review benchmark. The paper also documents scope creep and greater token use.
sources.limits: SWE-PRBench F1 uses model matching to human review comments, not complete bug truth. Prompt refinement on observed failures needs fresh hold-out validation. The text-constraint variant was not back-ported to the SWE-bench experiment. Do not transplant reported gains or round counts to this project.

access_notes: Search engines, community posts and secondary articles were discovery paths, not adopted technical-performance evidence.
Initial guessed Perplexity URLs failed; the numeric official help URL F02 was subsequently retrieved successfully.
The linked Microsoft technical-community article and PMLR PDF retrieval failed; claims are restricted to actually read original pages.
